faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?

faqs.q: What is the current National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. See the Fair Work Commission's order for details.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary?

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Understanding Your Pay

Whether you're negotiating a job offer or planning your budget, converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is a fundamental skill. In Australia, the standard assumption is a 38-hour week, but your actual hours may vary. This guide walks you through the calculation, explains the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and even compares your potential earnings to a well-known benchmark: the US president salary.

### The Basic Formula

The core calculation is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual figure is approximately $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This matches the Fair Work Commission's weekly rate of $1,004.90 multiplied by 52. The Fair Work Commission publishes the full National Minimum Wage Order 2026, which includes special rates for juniors, apprentices, and employees with disability.

If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. Part-time or casual employees might have fewer or irregular hours. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site lets you experiment with different inputs.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the National Minimum Wage example: $1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. This is useful for budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are quoted fortnightly.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most workers are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries or occupations. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) that list these rates. Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, evenings, or overtime, which can significantly boost annual earnings.

For instance, a hospitality worker under the Hospitality Industry General Award may earn a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage, plus additional loadings. Always check your award to ensure you're being paid correctly. The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool can help you find the right award and calculate your minimum pay.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. The Fair Work Commission's National Minimum Wage Order 2026 sets the casual rate at $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 + 25%). When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the "casual loading" box to add this automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – our tool handles the addition. For award-covered casuals, the loading may be specified in the award, often 25% or a different percentage.

### Superannuation

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. The rate is 12% for the 2026–27 year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to the employer. When estimating your total remuneration, include super. For example, on the National Minimum Wage annual salary of $52,245.44, the super contribution would be $6,269.45 (12%), making total employment cost $58,514.89. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator estimates these deductions, but note that it uses the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

### How Does Your Pay Compare to the US President Salary?

The US president's annual salary is a fixed $400,000 (as set by Congress). While that figure is far above most Australian incomes, it provides a useful benchmark. To earn $400,000 per year in Australia at a 38-hour week, you would need an hourly rate of approximately $400,000 ÷ (38 × 52) = $202.43 per hour. That's over seven times the National Minimum Wage. Of course, very few workers reach that level, but it illustrates how hourly rates scale.

More practically, you might compare your potential earnings to the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. That's roughly a quarter of the US president salary, but a more realistic target for many professionals.

### Using Our Tools

Our [timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Check the casual loading box if applicable. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) insights.

Remember, the annual figure is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

Converting your hourly rate to annual salary is straightforward: hourly × hours per week × 52. The National Minimum Wage sets the floor, but awards and enterprise agreements often provide higher rates. Casual workers get a 25% loading. Super is paid on top. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay. And if you're curious, the US president salary of $400,000 would require an hourly rate of over $200 – a useful perspective on income distribution.
